data.question: If all fish species were equally easy to farm, which ones would be more profitable?
data.answer_html:
That's a very interesting question.FALSE The profitability of fish farming depends on many factors, such as the market demand, the feed costs, the water quality, the temperature level, and the type of pond or system used.TRUE

[Y] Some of the most profitable fish to breed are dwarf cichlids, wild caught cichlids, discus, zebra pleco, clownfish, and yellow tang.TRUE [X] These fish are popular in aquariums and have high prices.TRUE However, they may also require more care and expertise to breed successfully.TRUE

Another profitable fish to farm is tilapia, which is one of the best-selling and most widely-eaten fish species in the world.TRUE Tilapia is easy to farm in warm water and has low feed costs.TRUE However, it may face competition from other producers and environmental concerns.TRUE

There are also many other fish species that can be profitable to farm depending on the location, the market, and the technology available.TRUE For example, some studies have shown that catfish, trout, striped bass, oysters, and clams are profitable in some regions.TRUE
data.claim_x: These fish are popular in aquariums and have high prices.
data.claim_y: Some of the most profitable fish to breed are dwarf cichlids, wild caught cichlids, discus, zebra pleco, clownfish, and yellow tang.
data.reading: Claim X is given as support for claim Y
